findings.description: User-authored split-test and release-gate expressions ran on the native backtracking regular-expression engine.
findings.evidence: Official Semgrep detect-non-literal-regexp identified native dynamic matching. A safe isolated Node subprocess testing ^/(a+)+$ against a 34-character path exceeded 2 seconds and was terminated. Input validation previously checked syntax only.
findings.impact: An authorized project operator or repository change could exhaust the CPU budget for a backtest or release check. Length-limiting the pattern alone did not prevent exponential matching.
findings.recommendation: Use RE2JS matching and validate the RE2 feature set at configuration boundaries. Existing patterns using lookaround/backreferences require replacement; stored gate configuration now fails explicitly instead of silently dropping ignores.
verification: 2026-10-25: 1000-character adversarial input completes through public weigh entry point; unsupported backreference syntax is rejected by gate and split-test schemas.
2026-10-25: DB-backed planCheck regression rejects unsupported stored gate config; saved split-test failures use actionable INVALID_PATH_PATTERN client copy.
2026-10-25: focused regression suite 105/105 passed across 22 files. Original native-regex findings in remediated paths absent from final Semgrep rescan.

Compatibility: RE2 matching preserves ordinary path search/anchors but intentionally rejects unsupported constructs. Recreate saved split tests with supported patterns; update relay-gate.json before retrying queued runs.

findings.description: Draft release notes used a predictable global temporary filename and followed pre-existing symlinks.
findings.evidence: CodeQL js/insecure-temporary-file reported the Date.now-based filename. A subprocess regression pre-created a symlink at that predictable name; original CLI overwrote the synthetic victim. Git and gh were local stubs and no release was published.
findings.impact: A different local user able to precreate the guessed temporary path could cause an operator running --draft to overwrite a writable file or alter temporary release-note handling.
findings.recommendation: Create a random private directory, exclusively write the note file with mode 0600, and remove the directory in a finally block.
verification: 2026-10-25: regression failed before patch by observing victim content replaced; passes after with unchanged victim,0700 directory, 0600 file, and cleanup.

findings.description: Wrangler .dev.vars credentials were included by COPY . . in self-host Docker images.
findings.evidence: Before the fix, an actual scratch Docker build using the repository ignore rules exported a synthetic .dev.vars file into its image. No real credential file was inspected or copied by this test.
findings.impact: Anyone able to read a locally built/published image could recover credentials from .dev.vars files present in the build context.
findings.recommendation: Exclude root and nested .dev.vars and environment variants from Docker contexts. If previous images were built with real secret files present, rotate the affected credentials and retire those images; removing files from a later image cannot revoke credentials.
verification: Before: synthetic Docker build exit0; exported .dev.vars exists=true.
Regression harness against HEAD Docker ignore rules failed with exit1; the same harness against patched rules passed with exit0.
After: python3 security/scanners/infrastructure-context-test.py passed;8 root/nested credential paths excluded;3 application/example files retained.
No claim is made that an existing published image contained credentials; rotation is conditional on historical image exposure.

findings.description: Three workflows inherited repository/organization token permissions instead of declaring the read-only permissions they require.
findings.evidence: Checkov3.3.30 reported3 CKV2_GHA_1 failures before the change; all3 files had no top-level permissions declaration. Actual repository/organization default token policy was not inspected.
findings.impact: Where repository defaults permit writes, compromised build steps could receive unnecessary GitHub token write privileges.
findings.recommendation: Set explicit permissions: contents: read, and request maintainer review of the workflow control-plane change.
verification: Before: security/reports/infrastructure-actions-before.json shows365 passed,3 failed,0 parsing errors.
After: security/reports/infrastructure-checkov-github-actions.json shows368 passed,0 failed,0 parsing errors.
Parent reviewed jobs and found no GitHub-token writes required; deployment credentials remain in existing explicit secrets.

findings.recommendation: Confirm staging headers and MIME behavior, then consider nosniff where compatible. Do not infer production configuration from Vite dev responses.

findings.description: CSP: Failure to Define Directive with No Fallback
findings.evidence: Observed Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'. src/server.ts appFetch intentionally applies framing protection without a script/style policy; no XSS was reproduced.
findings.impact: A restrictive CSP would limit the impact of a separate injection defect. This scan did not establish such a defect or verify deployed CDN/Worker headers.
findings.recommendation: Verify staging policy and design nonce-aware script restrictions compatible with TanStack bootstrap, Turnstile and PostHog before changing this policy.
verification: Agent E manually reviewed the healthy isolated hosted-mode development instance on 2026-10-25.
See security/reports/runtime-assessment.md for scope, evidence and limitations.

notes: No credential verification, remote Git fetch, or secret-bearing network request was performed.
Worktree scope: tracked and nonignored files; ignored local configuration, external symlinks, and generated reports are excluded.
History scope: all locally available Git references; unreachable objects and unfetched remote refs are not covered.
Raw output is temporary and private; report fields are allowlisted. No values, snippets, author emails, commit messages, or provider responses are retained.
False-positive decisions are exact file-content matches with explicit rationale, not scanner suppressions. Changed source requires new review.
Worktree snapshot contains 2924 files; snapshot is deleted after scanning.
Raw scanner artifacts stay in a private tools cache; committed outputs omit snippets and data-flow values.
A triage decision applies only to its exact source-file SHA-256; changed files return to unverified.
CodeQL licensing: public repositories are supported; private-repository use requires the appropriate GitHub Code Security entitlement.
Vulnerability severities come from advisories; production exploitability is not inferred solely from a package match.
Baseline findings persist as historical evidence. A fixed package finding requires a completed current audit of each originally affected workspace.
Cloudflare Wrangler JSONC, Alchemy TypeScript, and Compose are not covered by the installed native IaC policies; reviewed manually.
No cloud resources were deployed or queried. Image scanning uses only an existing local image and never pulls a target image.
Infrastructure reports omit source snippets, environment values, package URLs, and raw scanner logs.
Final snapshot contains manually validated false positives and fixed historical records; a fresh scanner run deliberately emits current detections for fresh triage.
A pre-existing Node CLI startup crash in auth-mode.ts was fixed with optional import.meta.env access; CLI regression failed before the fix and all19 related tests passed after.
Only explicitly authorized exact origin requested; no redirects followed.
Reports omit raw bodies, cookies, authorization headers, secrets, and query strings.
Scanner alerts require manual validation; findings are not marked fixed by this wrapper.
Assessment target: http://127.0.0.1:3217, isolated Vite development instance, own local D1, dummy providers, no production/staging systems scanned.
All 22 metadata alerts manually triaged; same-endpoint CSP subrules and Nuclei/ZAP nosniff observations deduplicate in the aggregate registry.
Four runtime safety tests pass. No confirmed runtime application vulnerability or runtime application fix is claimed.
